issues.claim: Using declarations are disposed at the end of the scope in reverse order of declaration (answer, explanation, optionExplanations.b)
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the using-statement page supports scope-end disposal for a using declaration. Its reverse-order sentence covers 'several instances in one using statement' (a comma-separated declaration list). It says nothing about several separate `using var` declarations. The second link (using-objects) does not mention order either. The explanation's detail that each later declaration is lowered to a try/finally nested inside the earlier one is also not shown in either excerpt. The answer is correct and the sandbox confirms 'body B A end', but no cited source shows the reverse order for using declarations.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the C# 8 'using declarations' proposal on Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/proposals/csharp-8.0/using) as a spec link, with matching ru/en linkTitles. Confirm that it states the lowering and the reverse-order disposal. If it does not, reword the explanation so it does not cite the docs for that point.

issues.claim: Как выглядел бы этот метод, если переписать оба объявления как обычные операторы `using` с блоками - какой блок оказался бы внутренним?
issues.problem: The hint almost spells out the mechanism (the later declaration is the inner block). It is acceptable as a nudge but close to the answer. The same applies to the en hint.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it, for example: 'Какой из двух ресурсов в обычных вложенных блоках using закрылся бы первым?' and the equivalent en wording.

issues.claim: В .NET 10 по умолчанию включена многоуровневая компиляция (tiered compilation)
issues.problem: The statement is true (default since .NET Core 3.0). Neither cited link covers tiered compilation, ReadyToRun or Native AOT, so these claims have no source in links.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally add https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/runtime-config/compilation as a link, with a title in both locales. Alternatively say 'tiered compilation is on by default' without tying it to .NET 10.

issues.problem: The fetched excerpt does not mention JIT by name. It does say the runtime uses metadata to generate native code, which supports the general claim that IL becomes native code at run time. The page is a general overview rather than the specific source for the first-call mechanism.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the link as a general reference. The managed-execution-process page is the real source for the stub and first-call mechanism.
